title: Flaky webkit explorer test: KBD-01/SR-01 fails intermittently in CI
description:
Filed by the opum-agent orchestrator session from CI evidence, not from a local repro.

`explorer browser qualification (chromium · firefox · webkit)` failed on PR #542 with
one webkit test red and 17 passing:

  [webkit] test/browser/explorer.pw.ts:34 KBD-01 and SR-01 provide complete keyboard
  and semantic detail flows -- failed at explorer.pw.ts:55

Line 55 reads the selected option's data-record-key, then focuses the close-details
button and presses Escape. chromium and firefox passed; only webkit failed.

PROVEN FLAKY, not a regression, by three independent facts:

1. The identical file content passed this exact check on PR #541 about twenty
   minutes earlier.
2. The change under test was an HTML comment in AGENTS.md. It cannot reach the
   static explorer UI.
3. Re-running the SAME job on the SAME commit (`gh run rerun 33810840103 --failed`)
   returned success. Same input, different result, is the definition.

Why it matters more than one red square. lore-cli is the fleet repository that gates
`dev` rather than `main`, and `dev`'s ruleset requires three checks on every push.
A test that fails intermittently on a ref whose ruleset blocks pushes is a
periodic, unexplained wall in front of every landing, and the natural response --
re-run until green -- is also exactly how a real webkit-only regression would be
waved through. The two are indistinguishable from the outside once re-running is
habit.

Suggested direction: make the assertion at explorer.pw.ts:55 wait for the state it
reads rather than sampling it, and check whether the aria-selected option is
settled before getAttribute. A webkit-only failure in a keyboard/focus flow is
usually a focus or a11y-tree timing race rather than a logic error.

Run: https://github.com/opum-ai/lore-cli/actions/runs/33810840103

acceptanceCriteria.text: The KBD-01/SR-01 webkit test passes on 20 consecutive CI runs, or its race is fixed at the assertion
The fix waits for state rather than lengthening a timeout

plan: 1. Trace explorer.ts's closeDetails(key): state.selected=null; render(); focusRecord(key) -- render() rebuilds BOTH #nodes (all option buttons, including the target) AND, via its trailing renderDetails() call, #details (which destroys the currently-focused "Close details" button -- the very element whose own keydown handler is mid-execution).

2. Diagnose: this is a same-tick destroy-the-focused-element-then-focus-a-different-element race. Chromium/Firefox settle it synchronously; a WebKit build (this repos CI runs Linux webkit) can drop the .focus() call when it races the browsers own internal focus-cleanup for the removed node -- matching whywebkit-only, why re-running the same commit flips outcome, and why Playwrights 5s toBeFocused() retry does not reliably save it (the call can be lost, not merely delayed).

3. Fix at the root: defer closeDetails focusRecord(key) call to requestAnimationFrame, so it runs after the browser has settled the prior elements removal -- waits for real state (a frame boundary), not an arbitrary timeout (AC2).

4. Verify: full explorer.pw.ts suite across chromium/firefox/webkit locally (18/18 pass), explorer unit/contract/qualification suites (20/20), full bun test (2802/2802), typecheck, lint -- all clean. Docker/CI-shaped Linux webkit unavailable locally, so cannot reproduce the original flake directly; the fix targets the mechanism, not a symptom.
implementationNotes: Root cause identified in src/core/explorer.ts: closeDetails(key) is the ONLY focus-after-keyboard-interaction path in this test that calls render() (which destroys and rebuilds both #nodes and #details) BEFORE calling focusRecord(key) -- i.e. it destroys the currently-focused close-details button as part of its own keydown handler, then synchronously tries to focus a different, freshly-created button in a different panel. This exact hazard also exists at two OTHER call sites with the identical shape (state mutation; render(); focusRecord(...)): the clear-focus button handler (line ~265) and the "Focus this record" button click handler inside renderDetails (line ~278). Neither is exercised by an explorer.pw.ts toBeFocused() assertion today, so I did not touch them -- flagging as a plausible sibling accessibility bug worth its own task if anyone hits it, not fixing speculatively here. Fix applied: closeDetails now defers its focusRecord call via requestAnimationFrame. Verified locally across chromium/firefox/webkit (18/18 browser tests), full unit suite (2802/2802), typecheck, lint. Could not reproduce the original Linux-webkit-only flake locally (this sandbox has no Docker / Linux webkit); CI is the real test per AC1'\''s own escape hatch (20 consecutive green runs).
